THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 87

After some words of thanks by the president, the audience was quietly dismissed, and we are sure that all went away much edified and improved. The subscription was fifty cents a year or twenty-five cents for five months.

THE CICERONIAN DEBATING SOCIETY—Mr. Geo. W. McKee, of Bells, Texas, recalls that he was a member of the College debating society named, after some discussion, "The Ciceronian," was organized. Whether this organization supplanted one of the older societies or supplemented the work of both is not remembered, as the recollections of other persons consulted are somewhat conflicting. From the name suggests, by the same Mr. McKee. At the Philomathean Society seems to have been more lively than the Ciceronian Society seems to have become extinct, making it necessary for a successor at the College to seek such a successor at the College. It may be noted, however, that all who had a part in creating such a successor were justly proud of the results; and the Ciceronian Society would have never renewed; so the Ciceronian group could have been a rival to the other.
